title: Perceptron and Artificial Neurons
overview: A neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias and passes it through a nonlinearity. The perceptron is the simplest case and the building block of every deep network.

title: Multilayer Perceptron and Backpropagation
overview: Stacking layers of neurons with nonlinearities lets a network model complex functions. Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute the gradient of the loss for every weight efficiently.

title: Activation Functions
overview: Activation functions inject nonlinearity so networks can learn more than linear maps. The choice affects gradient flow, convergence speed and output range.

title: Loss Functions
overview: A loss function turns prediction error into a single number the optimizer can minimize. Matching the loss to the task and output distribution matters for stable training.

title: Optimizers: SGD, Momentum and Adam
overview: Optimizers decide how gradients become parameter updates. Momentum and adaptive methods like Adam speed up and stabilize training compared with plain SGD.

title: Initialization and Normalization
overview: Good initialization keeps activations and gradients at a sensible scale, and normalization layers keep them there during training. Together they make deep networks trainable.

title: Regularization: Dropout, Weight Decay, Early Stopping
overview: Deep networks can memorize training data. Regularization techniques constrain the model or training procedure so it generalizes better to unseen data.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks
overview: Convolutional layers slide small shared filters over an image, exploiting locality and translation structure. They need far fewer parameters than fully connected layers on images.

title: Classic CNN Architectures: LeNet, VGG, ResNet
overview: The history of CNN design shows how depth, small filters and skip connections made image models both deeper and easier to train.

title: Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning
overview: Reusing a network pretrained on a large dataset gives strong features with little labeled data. You can freeze the backbone or fine-tune it with a small learning rate.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks
overview: Recurrent networks process sequences one step at a time while carrying a hidden state. They share weights across time but struggle with long-range dependencies.

title: LSTM and GRU
overview: Gated recurrent cells control what to remember and forget, giving gradients a more stable path through time. LSTM and GRU are the standard recurrent building blocks.

title: Sequence-to-Sequence and Attention
overview: Encoder-decoder models map one sequence to another, such as translation. Attention lets the decoder look back at all encoder states instead of one fixed vector.

title: Transformers
overview: Transformers replace recurrence with self-attention, letting every token attend to every other token in parallel. They underpin most modern language, vision and multimodal models.

title: BERT and GPT Style Language Models
overview: Pretrained transformer language models learn from large text corpora. BERT-style encoders predict masked tokens for understanding tasks, while GPT-style decoders predict the next token for generation.

title: Autoencoders
overview: An autoencoder compresses inputs into a low-dimensional code and reconstructs them. The bottleneck forces the network to learn useful structure without labels.

title: Interpretability of Deep Networks
overview: Interpretability methods help us understand why a network produced a prediction. Gradient-based attributions, attention inspection and probing each give partial, imperfect evidence.

title: Model Compression: Pruning, Quantization, Distillation
overview: Compression makes models smaller and faster for deployment. Pruning removes weights, quantization lowers numeric precision and distillation trains a small student to mimic a larger teacher.

title: Variational Autoencoders
overview: A VAE learns a probabilistic latent space: the encoder outputs a distribution rather than a point. Sampling from the prior then lets the decoder generate new data.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks
overview: A GAN trains a generator and a discriminator in a minimax game. The generator learns to produce samples the discriminator cannot tell from real data.

title: Diffusion Models
overview: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process. Sampling starts from pure noise and denoises step by step to produce data.

title: Graph Neural Networks
overview: Graph neural networks learn from nodes and edges by passing messages between neighbors. They suit molecules, social networks and other relational data.

title: Self-Supervised and Contrastive Learning
overview: Self-supervised learning builds training signals from the data itself, so large unlabeled datasets can teach useful representations. Contrastive methods pull together views of the same example and push apart others.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning
overview: Deep reinforcement learning uses neural networks to approximate value functions or policies, learning from rewards through interaction. DQN and policy gradients are two foundational families.

title: Distributed and Mixed-Precision Training
overview: Large models need many GPUs and efficient numerics. Data and model parallelism split the work, while mixed precision uses 16-bit math to save memory and time.
